summary: Cameron David Warner is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD at Harvard University and studied under Yudru Tsomu. He held academic posts at Middlebury College and Dickinson College.
Cameron Kyle Bender Foltz works in religious studies and Sinology. He earned an MA at Florida State University under the supervision of Bryan J. Cuevas (attested 2018).

Camillo Alessio Formigatti specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Milan and the University of Hamburg (PhD attested 2011), he held posts at Cambridge (2011–2014), SOAS, the University of Oxford (attested 2017), and the Bodleian Library.
Carel Gabriel Cobet (1813–1889) was a Dutch linguist who studied at the Gymnasium Haganum and Leiden University. He later held posts as a professor at Leiden University in 1846 and from 1849 to 1884.

Carl A. P. Ruck is a scholar in religious studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Michigan (~1958–1960) and Harvard University (~1960–1965), and held a post at Boston University around 1970.

Carl Bielefeldt specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied under Shunryu Suzuki and Seizan Yanagida, earning his PhD from UC Berkeley (~1972–1980), and held posts at Stanford University (~1980) and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

Carl Cappeller (1840–1925) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Berlin under Franz Bopp and Albrecht Weber, completed his PhD at Leipzig and Habilitation at Jena, and served as professor at the University of Jena from 1875.

Carl Christian Rafn (1795–1864) was a Danish scholar in history, archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen (~1814–1816) and subsequently held a post there from circa 1820 to 1864.

Carl Darling Buck (1866–1955) was an American linguist who studied at Yale University (~1882–1889) and the University of Leipzig (~1889–1892). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago from 1892 to 1933.
Carl Gaedicke (born 1853) studied under Carl Cappeller and Berthold Delbrück, completing his PhD at the University of Jena by 1877.

Carl Gustav Jung (1875–1961) studied medicine at the University of Basel (1895–1900). In the fields of religious studies and psychology, he held academic posts at the University of Zurich, ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and the University of Basel (1944).

Carl Olson is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied under mentor John Y. Fenton. He held the Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).
Carl Paul Caspari (1814–1892) was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Leipzig and Berlin, and served as a lektor (1847) and professor (1857) at the University of Oslo.

Carl Schuster (1904–1969) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Sinology. He pursued his studies at Harvard University from approximately 1923 to 1930 and at the University of Vienna from approximately 1930 to 1934.
Carl Shigeo Yamamoto is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he studied under Jeffrey Hopkins and David F. Germano.

Carl Siegfried (1830–1903) was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Albrecht Weber, Rudolf von Roth, and Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker. He held posts at Schulpforta, Trinity College Dublin, and the University of Jena (~1875–1903).

Carl W. Ernst is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Stanford and Harvard (PhD 1981). He taught at Pomona College (1981–1992) and was a professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff (1876–1967) was a linguist and archaeologist. After studying at Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin (PhD ~1901), he held professorships in Greek language and literature at the University of Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht University (1917–1946).

Carlo Formichi (1871–1943) was an Italian Indologist. He studied under Michele Kerbaker, Paul Deussen, Hermann Oldenberg, and Georg Bühler, later serving as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (1898) and the University of Rome (1914–1941).

Carlo Giussani (1840–1900) studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863) under Giuseppe Bardelli. He also studied under Albrecht Weber in 1863 and Rudolf von Roth from approximately 1865 to 1866.
